nodes.label: Order of magnitude
nodes.description: Rounds a value to the nearest power of ten so that very different scales can be compared multiplicatively.

nodes.label: SI system of units
nodes.description: The convention that fixes base quantities and their units and builds every other unit as a product of powers of them.
properties: seven base units (s, m, kg, A, K, mol, cd)
derived unit = product of powers of base units

nodes.label: Time
nodes.description: Read from a clock. SI unit the second, fixed by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency.

nodes.label: Length
nodes.description: Read from a ruler. SI unit the metre, fixed by the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299 792 458 s.

nodes.label: Mass
nodes.description: Inertial measure of the amount of matter, read from a balance. SI unit the kilogram, fixed since 2019 through Planck's constant.

nodes.label: Unit conversion
nodes.description: Multiplies a quantity by a ratio equal to one, so the number changes and the quantity does not.

nodes.label: Dimensional analysis
nodes.description: Tracks the powers of base dimensions in a quantity; an equation is admissible only if both sides carry the same dimension.
properties: dimensions form a multiplicative group generated by L, M, T, …
only like dimensions add or equate
arguments of exp, sin, log are dimensionless

nodes.label: Estimation (Fermi)
nodes.description: Obtains an order-of-magnitude answer from rough inputs combined in a dimensionally consistent way.

nodes.label: Discrepancy
nodes.description: Difference between a measured value and the accepted value; a small discrepancy means high accuracy.

nodes.label: Uncertainty
nodes.description: The spread of a measured value; percent uncertainty δA/A·100 % compares it with the value itself. Small spread means high precision.

nodes.label: Uncertainty propagation
nodes.description: For products and quotients the percent uncertainties add (to first order), which bounds the uncertainty of a result.

nodes.label: Significant figures
nodes.description: Bookkeeping rule that keeps only the digits supported by the uncertainty of the inputs.
properties: × and ÷ keep the fewest significant figures
+ and − keep the fewest decimal places

nodes.label: Scalar
nodes.description: A quantity fixed by one real number and a unit; scalars obey ordinary arithmetic.
properties: addition and multiplication commutative and associative
equations between scalars are scalar equations

nodes.label: Vector
nodes.description: A quantity with magnitude and direction; displacement is the model case. Two vectors can be parallel, antiparallel or orthogonal.
properties: a vector equation fixes magnitude and direction at once

nodes.label: Vector addition
nodes.description: Combines vectors head to tail (or by the parallelogram) into a resultant; subtraction adds the antiparallel vector.

nodes.label: Multiplication by a scalar
nodes.description: Stretches a vector by |α| and reverses it if α < 0; dividing a vector by its magnitude gives a unit vector.
properties: distributive over vector and scalar sums

nodes.label: Vector components
nodes.symbol: A⃗ = A_x î + A_y ĵ + A_z k̂
nodes.description: Writes a vector in the orthonormal basis of a Cartesian coordinate system; vector equations become one scalar equation per axis.

nodes.label: Polar coordinates
nodes.description: Locates a point in a plane by its distance from the origin and an angle from the x-axis.
properties: x = r cos φ, y = r sin φ

nodes.label: Scalar product
nodes.description: Multiplies two vectors into a scalar, AB cos φ; it projects one vector on another and vanishes for orthogonal vectors.

nodes.label: Vector product
nodes.description: Multiplies two vectors into a vector perpendicular to both, of magnitude AB sin φ, oriented by the right-hand rule.

nodes.label: Position
nodes.description: Coordinate of the body on an axis of the frame at a given instant.

nodes.label: Reference frame
nodes.description: An origin and axes against which positions are measured, together with a clock.
properties: choice of origin and axes arbitrary

nodes.label: Motion on a line
nodes.description: The kinematic state of a body on a line: its position at every instant.
nodes.math_structure: function t ↦ x(t), ℝ → ℝ

nodes.label: Displacement
nodes.description: Change of position between two instants; signed. A total displacement is the sum of successive displacements.

nodes.label: Distance traveled
nodes.description: Total length of path covered, never negative; it can exceed the magnitude of the displacement.

nodes.label: Average velocity
nodes.description: Displacement divided by the elapsed time; it depends only on the end points of the interval.

nodes.label: Elapsed time
nodes.description: Duration of an interval between two clock readings.

nodes.label: Time derivative
nodes.description: The limit of a difference quotient as the interval shrinks; turns a quantity known at every instant into its rate of change.

nodes.label: Instantaneous velocity
nodes.description: Rate of change of position at an instant: the slope of x(t).

nodes.label: Average speed
nodes.description: Distance traveled divided by elapsed time.

nodes.label: Speed
nodes.description: Magnitude of the instantaneous velocity.

nodes.label: Average acceleration
nodes.description: Change of velocity divided by elapsed time.

nodes.label: Instantaneous acceleration
nodes.description: Rate of change of velocity: the slope of v(t), the curvature of x(t).

nodes.label: Constant-acceleration kinematics
nodes.description: The motion when acceleration does not change: velocity linear and position quadratic in time.
properties: polynomial of degree two in t

nodes.label: Free fall
nodes.description: Vertical motion with acceleration −g; Galileo's result that the motion does not depend on the mass.
properties: special case a = −g of constant-acceleration kinematics

nodes.label: Free-fall acceleration
nodes.description: Acceleration of a body falling near Earth's surface without air resistance: about 9.80 m/s², the same for all bodies at one place.

nodes.label: Time integral
nodes.description: Accumulates a rate over time; undoes the derivative up to a constant fixed by initial conditions.
properties: ∫ (d f/dt) dt = f + C (fundamental theorem of calculus)

nodes.label: Position vector
nodes.description: Vector from the origin of the frame to the body: r⃗ = x î + y ĵ + z k̂.

nodes.label: Trajectory
nodes.description: The kinematic state in space: the curve traced by the position vector, made of three independent motions along the axes.
nodes.math_structure: curve t ↦ r⃗(t) in ℝ³

nodes.label: Displacement vector
nodes.description: Change of the position vector between two instants.

nodes.label: Velocity vector
nodes.description: Rate of change of the position vector; tangent to the trajectory.

nodes.label: Acceleration vector
nodes.description: Rate of change of the velocity vector; in curved motion it has parts across and along the path (total acceleration).

nodes.label: Projectile motion
nodes.description: Motion under gravity alone: uniform horizontally, free fall vertically, the two independent.
properties: parabolic trajectory y = (tan θ₀)x − g x²/(2v₀² cos²θ₀)

nodes.label: Time of flight
nodes.description: Time a projectile spends in the air.

nodes.label: Range
nodes.description: Horizontal distance traveled by a projectile landing at its launch height.

nodes.label: Circular motion
nodes.description: The state of a body moving on a circle of radius r: its angle at every instant.
nodes.math_structure: curve on a circle S¹ ⊂ ℝ²: r⃗(t) = r(cos φ(t), sin φ(t))

nodes.label: Centripetal acceleration
nodes.description: Acceleration toward the centre needed to keep a body on a circle.

nodes.label: Angular frequency
nodes.description: Rate at which the angle advances, in rad/s; constant in uniform circular motion.

nodes.label: Tangential acceleration
nodes.description: Rate of change of speed; directed along the path.

nodes.label: Relative motion
nodes.description: Converts positions and velocities between two reference frames in relative motion by adding the frames' relative position and velocity.
properties: vector addition of relative positions, velocities and accelerations
time is the same in all frames
acceleration is frame-independent for frames moving uniformly

nodes.label: Relative velocity
nodes.description: Velocity of a body measured in a frame that itself moves.

nodes.label: Force
nodes.description: A push or pull on a body, with magnitude and direction; measured by the stretch of a calibrated spring. SI unit the newton, 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

nodes.label: Free-body diagram
nodes.description: Isolates one body and draws every external force on it as a vector from the body; the starting point of every force problem.
properties: separates the system from its surroundings

nodes.label: Net external force
nodes.description: Vector sum of all external forces on a body.

nodes.label: Newton's first law
nodes.description: A body keeps its velocity unless a net external force acts; this tendency is inertia, measured by mass.
properties: defines the class of inertial frames
special case F⃗_net = 0 of the second law

nodes.label: Inertial reference frame
nodes.description: A frame in which the first law holds; any frame moving at constant velocity relative to one is also inertial.
properties: closed under constant-velocity changes of frame

nodes.label: Newton's second law
nodes.description: The net external force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration; one equation per component.
properties: second order in time, so r⃗₀ and v⃗₀ fix the motion

nodes.label: Weight
nodes.description: Gravitational force of the Earth on a body near its surface; proportional to mass, unlike mass itself it depends on location.

nodes.label: Newton's third law
nodes.description: Forces come in pairs: when A pushes on B, B pushes back on A with an equal and opposite force. The two act on different bodies.
properties: internal forces of a system cancel in pairs

nodes.label: Normal force
nodes.description: Contact force perpendicular to a surface, as large as needed to stop the body from moving into it.

nodes.label: Tension
nodes.description: Pulling force transmitted along a string or cable.

nodes.label: Hooke's law
nodes.description: A spring pulls back with a force proportional to its stretch from the relaxed length.

nodes.label: Friction law
nodes.description: Contact force parallel to a surface that opposes relative motion (kinetic) or its onset (static), proportional to the normal force.

nodes.label: Static friction
nodes.description: Friction between surfaces not sliding relative to each other; adjusts up to a maximum μ_s N.

nodes.label: Kinetic friction
nodes.description: Friction between sliding surfaces, opposite to the relative velocity.

nodes.label: Centripetal force
nodes.description: Net force toward the centre that a circular motion requires; supplied by tension, friction, gravity or a normal force.

nodes.label: Banked curve
nodes.description: A road tilted so the horizontal part of the normal force supplies the centripetal force at a design speed.

nodes.label: Noninertial frame
nodes.description: An accelerating or rotating frame; the laws of motion hold there only if inertial (fictitious) forces such as the centrifugal force are added.

nodes.label: Coriolis force
nodes.description: Inertial force on a body moving relative to a rotating frame, perpendicular to its velocity; deflects winds and projectiles on Earth.

nodes.label: Drag force
nodes.description: Resistance of a fluid to a body moving through it; grows with the square of speed for fast motion, linearly for slow motion in viscous fluid.

nodes.label: Terminal velocity
nodes.description: Constant speed reached when the drag force balances the weight.

nodes.label: Work
nodes.description: Energy transferred by a force acting along a displacement; only the component of force along the path does work. SI unit the joule.

nodes.label: Kinetic energy
nodes.description: Energy of motion of a particle; depends on the frame through the speed.

nodes.label: Net work
nodes.description: Work done by the net force, equal to the sum of the works of all forces.

nodes.label: Work–energy theorem
nodes.description: The net work done on a particle equals its change of kinetic energy.
properties: scalar consequence of the second law
the path enters only through W_net

nodes.label: Power
nodes.description: Rate at which work is done; P = F⃗·v⃗ for a force acting on a moving body. Average power is work over elapsed time.

nodes.label: Potential energy
nodes.description: Energy of a system stored in its configuration; only differences are physical, so the zero can be chosen freely.

nodes.label: Gravitational potential energy (near Earth)
nodes.description: Potential energy of the body–Earth system for a height y near the surface.

nodes.label: Elastic potential energy
nodes.description: Potential energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring.

nodes.label: Conservative force
nodes.description: A force whose work between two points is independent of the path; equivalently zero around every closed path, and derivable from a potential energy.
properties: gravity and springs conservative, friction not

nodes.label: Work of nonconservative forces
nodes.description: Work by forces such as friction or air resistance, which depends on the path and changes the mechanical energy.

nodes.label: Mechanical energy
nodes.description: Kinetic plus potential energy of a system.

nodes.label: Conservation of mechanical energy
nodes.description: Mechanical energy changes only through the work of nonconservative forces; without them it is a conserved quantity.
properties: follows from the work–energy theorem with W_cons = −ΔU
energy lost to friction becomes thermal energy

nodes.label: Potential-energy diagram
nodes.description: A plot of U(x) with the total energy as a horizontal line; motion is allowed only where E ≥ U, and reverses at turning points.

nodes.label: Equilibrium point
nodes.description: A position where the force vanishes; stable at a minimum of U (small disturbances oscillate), unstable at a maximum.
nodes.math_structure: point x₀ with U′(x₀) = 0; stable if U″(x₀) > 0

nodes.label: Momentum
nodes.description: Mass times velocity; a vector.

nodes.label: Impulse
nodes.description: Time integral of a force; for a short collision, average force times duration.

nodes.label: Impulse–momentum theorem
nodes.description: The impulse of the net force equals the change of momentum.
properties: integral form of the second law
independent of the detailed force history

nodes.label: System of particles
nodes.description: A chosen set of bodies; forces split into internal (between members) and external. A closed system has no net external force.
nodes.math_structure: N labelled trajectories r⃗_j(t) ∈ ℝ³ with masses m_j

nodes.label: Conservation of momentum
nodes.description: The total momentum of a closed system does not change, whatever happens inside it.

nodes.label: Collisions
nodes.description: Collisions conserve momentum; they are classified by kinetic energy: elastic (kept), inelastic (lost), perfectly inelastic (bodies stick together), explosion (gained).
properties: kinetic energy conserved only in elastic collisions
perfectly inelastic loses the most K compatible with P

nodes.label: Center of mass
nodes.description: Mass-weighted average position of a system; for a continuous body r⃗_CM = (1/M)∫ r⃗ dm.

nodes.label: Second law for a system
nodes.description: The centre of mass moves like a single particle of total mass M acted on by the external forces alone.
properties: reduces many-body motion to one point plus internal motion

nodes.label: Linear mass density
nodes.description: Mass per unit length of a rod or string; used to integrate over continuous bodies.

nodes.label: Rocket equation
nodes.description: A rocket gains speed by ejecting mass backward at exhaust speed u; the gain depends on the logarithm of the mass ratio.
properties: independent of burn rate in free space

nodes.label: Rigid body on a fixed axis
nodes.description: A body whose particles keep their mutual distances, turning about a fixed axis: every particle moves on a circle and one angle describes them all.
nodes.math_structure: one angle θ(t) ∈ S¹ (one degree of freedom); each particle on a circle of fixed radius r_j

nodes.label: Angular position
nodes.description: Angle of a reference line of the body from a fixed direction, in radians: arc length over radius.

nodes.label: Angular velocity
nodes.description: Rate of change of angular position; as a vector it points along the axis by the right-hand rule. Tangential speed v_t = rω.

nodes.label: Angular acceleration
nodes.description: Rate of change of angular velocity; tangential acceleration of a point is a_t = rα.

nodes.label: Rotational kinematics
nodes.description: Equations for rotation at constant angular acceleration, the same form as the linear ones with θ, ω, α in place of x, v, a.

nodes.label: Rotational kinetic energy
nodes.description: Kinetic energy of a rotating rigid body, the sum of ½m_j v_j² with v_j = r_jω.

nodes.label: Moment of inertia
nodes.description: Rotational inertia: how mass is distributed about the axis. Depends on the axis chosen.

nodes.label: Parallel-axis theorem
nodes.description: The moment of inertia about any axis equals that about the parallel axis through the centre of mass plus Md².
properties: I_CM is the minimum over parallel axes
moments of a compound body add

nodes.label: Surface mass density
nodes.description: Mass per unit area of a thin sheet or disk.

nodes.label: Torque
nodes.description: The turning effect of a force about a point or axis: force times lever arm, |τ| = r⊥F, signed by the right-hand rule.

nodes.label: Second law for rotation
nodes.description: Net torque about a fixed axis equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration.

nodes.label: Rotational work
nodes.description: Work done by a torque as the body turns.

nodes.label: Rolling without slipping
nodes.description: A wheel rolls without slipping when its contact point is instantaneously at rest; translation and rotation are then locked together.

nodes.label: Angular momentum
nodes.description: Moment of momentum about a point; for a rigid body rotating about a symmetry axis, L = Iω.

nodes.label: Torque law
nodes.description: The rate of change of angular momentum equals the net external torque.
properties: internal torques cancel for central internal forces

nodes.label: Conservation of angular momentum
nodes.description: With no net external torque, the total angular momentum is constant; a skater who pulls in her arms (smaller I) spins faster.
properties: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂ for a body changing shape
book_terms: law of conservation of angular momentum

nodes.label: Precession rate
nodes.description: Slow turning of a spinning top's axis, because gravity's torque changes the direction of L⃗ rather than its size.

nodes.label: Static equilibrium
nodes.description: A rigid body at rest that stays at rest; it has no translational and no rotational acceleration.
nodes.math_structure: configuration of a rigid body with ΣF⃗ = 0 and Στ⃗ = 0 about every point

nodes.label: Equilibrium conditions
nodes.description: The first condition (zero net force) prevents translation; the second (zero net torque) prevents rotation.
properties: if both hold, the torque condition holds about any point

nodes.label: Center of gravity
nodes.description: Point where the total weight can be taken to act; it coincides with the centre of mass in a uniform gravitational field.

nodes.label: Stress
nodes.description: Force per unit area that deforms a body: tensile or compressive (perpendicular), bulk (from all sides), shear (parallel to the surface).

nodes.label: Strain
nodes.description: Fractional deformation: change of length, volume or shear offset divided by the original size; dimensionless.

nodes.label: Linear elasticity
nodes.description: For small deformations stress is proportional to strain; the constant is the elastic modulus of the material for that kind of deformation.

nodes.label: Young's modulus
nodes.description: Elastic modulus for tension or compression along one direction.

nodes.label: Bulk modulus
nodes.description: Elastic modulus for uniform compression; its inverse is the compressibility.

nodes.label: Shear modulus
nodes.description: Elastic modulus for shear deformation.

nodes.label: Pressure
nodes.description: Perpendicular force per unit area; a scalar. SI unit the pascal, 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

nodes.label: Stress–strain diagram
nodes.description: A material is linear up to the proportionality limit, elastic (returns to shape) up to the elastic limit, plastic beyond it, and breaks at the ultimate stress.

nodes.label: Gravitational constant
nodes.description: Strength of gravity between two masses, 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg², first measured with a torsion balance (Cavendish).

nodes.label: Newton's law of gravitation
nodes.description: Every pair of point masses attracts along the line joining them with a force proportional to both masses and inversely to the square of the distance.
properties: a spherical shell acts as a point mass at its centre

nodes.label: Gravitational field
nodes.description: Gravitational force per unit mass at a point; it exists whether or not a test mass is there.

nodes.label: Apparent weight
nodes.description: What a scale reads: the normal force, which differs from mg in an accelerating or rotating frame (reduced at the equator by Earth's rotation).

nodes.label: Gravitational potential energy
nodes.description: Potential energy of two masses at any separation, with zero at infinite separation; near Earth's surface it reduces to mgy.

nodes.label: Escape velocity
nodes.description: Minimum launch speed for a body to move off to infinite distance.

nodes.label: Gravitationally bound orbit
nodes.description: A system whose total energy is negative cannot separate to infinity; the bodies stay within a maximum distance.
nodes.math_structure: trajectory confined to r ≤ r_max; total energy E < 0 (E = −GMm/2r on a circle)

nodes.label: Orbital speed
nodes.description: Speed of a circular orbit at radius r; independent of the satellite's mass.

nodes.label: Orbital period
nodes.description: Time for one circular orbit.

nodes.label: Kepler's first law
nodes.symbol: orbit = ellipse, Sun at a focus
nodes.description: Every planet moves on an ellipse with the Sun at one focus; derived by Newton from the inverse-square law.
properties: conic sections α/r = 1 + e cos θ

nodes.label: Elliptical orbit
nodes.description: The orbital state: an ellipse traced periodically, closest to the Sun at perihelion and farthest at aphelion.
nodes.math_structure: conic section with eccentricity e < 1, semimajor axis a; closed periodic curve

nodes.label: Kepler's second law
nodes.description: The line from Sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times, so a planet moves fastest at perihelion.
properties: equivalent to conservation of angular momentum for a central force

nodes.label: Kepler's third law
nodes.description: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semimajor axis.
properties: same constant for all planets of one star
independent of planet mass (when m ≪ M)

nodes.label: Tidal force
nodes.description: Difference in the gravitational pull across a body; it stretches the body along the line to the attracting mass. Sun and Moon aligned give spring tides, at right angles neap tides.

nodes.label: Speed of light
nodes.description: Speed of light in vacuum, 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s (exact by the definition of the metre).

nodes.label: General relativity
nodes.description: Gravity is the curvature of space-time produced by mass and energy; free bodies follow the straightest paths of the curved geometry.
properties: reduces to Newton's law for weak fields and slow motion

nodes.label: Principle of equivalence
nodes.description: No local experiment can distinguish a uniform gravitational field from an accelerated frame; a freely falling frame is locally inertial.
properties: free fall replaces the inertial frame

nodes.label: Black hole
nodes.description: A mass compressed inside its Schwarzschild radius; nothing, not even light, escapes from inside the event horizon.
nodes.math_structure: space-time region bounded by the event horizon r = R_S

nodes.label: Schwarzschild radius
nodes.description: Radius at which the escape velocity from a mass M reaches the speed of light; it marks the event horizon.

nodes.label: Fluid
nodes.description: A liquid or gas: matter that flows because it cannot resist a shear stress when at rest; described by fields such as density and pressure.
nodes.math_structure: continuum: scalar fields ρ(r⃗, t), p(r⃗, t) on a region of ℝ³

nodes.label: Density
nodes.description: Mass per unit volume.

nodes.label: Specific gravity
nodes.description: Density relative to that of water; dimensionless.

nodes.label: Gauge and absolute pressure
nodes.description: Gauges read pressure relative to the atmosphere; absolute pressure adds atmospheric pressure.

nodes.label: Hydrostatic equilibrium
nodes.description: In a fluid at rest pressure grows with depth so that each fluid element is balanced: p = p₀ + ρgh for constant density.
properties: ρ constant ⇒ p linear in depth
pressure depends only on depth, not container shape

nodes.label: Pascal's principle
nodes.description: A pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid reaches every part of it; a hydraulic jack multiplies force by the area ratio.

nodes.label: Buoyant force
nodes.description: Net upward force of a fluid on an immersed body.

nodes.label: Archimedes' principle
nodes.description: A body immersed in a fluid is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.
properties: body floats if its mean density < fluid density

nodes.label: Ideal fluid
nodes.description: A model fluid with constant density and no internal friction; its steady flow is laminar.

nodes.label: Viscosity
nodes.description: Internal friction of a fluid: the shear stress needed per velocity gradient.

nodes.label: Fluid flow
nodes.description: The motion of a fluid: a velocity at every point. In laminar flow the layers slide smoothly; in turbulent flow eddies mix them.
nodes.math_structure: vector field v⃗(r⃗, t) on the fluid region; streamlines tangent to v⃗

nodes.label: Flow rate
nodes.description: Volume of fluid passing a cross section per unit time.

nodes.label: Continuity equation
nodes.description: Mass entering a flow tube equals mass leaving; for an incompressible fluid A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, so the flow speeds up where the tube narrows.

nodes.label: Bernoulli's equation
nodes.description: Along a streamline of an ideal fluid, pressure plus kinetic and potential energy per volume is constant; faster flow means lower pressure (Bernoulli's principle).
properties: valid for steady, incompressible, nonviscous flow

nodes.label: Poiseuille's law
nodes.description: Laminar viscous flow through a tube: flow rate is the pressure difference over a resistance R = 8ηl/(πr⁴).
properties: resistance analogous to an electrical resistance

nodes.label: Reynolds number
nodes.description: Dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous effects; flow in a tube is laminar below about 2000 and turbulent above about 3000.

nodes.label: Period
nodes.description: Time for one cycle of a periodic motion (an oscillation).

nodes.label: Frequency
nodes.description: Number of cycles per unit time; SI unit the hertz.

nodes.label: Simple harmonic oscillator
nodes.description: A mass on an ideal spring: the restoring force is proportional to displacement, giving simple harmonic motion.

nodes.label: Harmonic oscillation
nodes.description: The oscillator's state: amplitude A and phase shift φ about the equilibrium position; equivalently the pair (x, v) at one instant.
nodes.math_structure: (A, φ) ∈ [0, ∞) × S¹; equivalently a point (x, v) on an ellipse in the phase plane

nodes.label: Force constant
nodes.description: Stiffness of a spring: force per unit stretch, in N/m.

nodes.label: Restoring force
nodes.description: Force that pushes a body back toward a stable equilibrium point; linear for small displacements.

nodes.label: Simple pendulum
nodes.description: A point mass on a light string; for small angles it is a harmonic oscillator whose period depends only on length and g.
properties: period independent of mass and (small) amplitude

nodes.label: Physical pendulum
nodes.description: An extended body swinging about a pivot; its period depends on its moment of inertia and the distance L from pivot to centre of mass.
properties: reduces to the simple pendulum for I = mL²

nodes.label: Torsional pendulum
nodes.description: A body twisting on a wire whose restoring torque is proportional to the twist angle.
properties: exact harmonic motion for elastic twist

nodes.label: Damped oscillator
nodes.description: An oscillator with a drag force proportional to velocity; it is underdamped (decaying oscillation), critically damped or overdamped (no oscillation).
properties: underdamped b² < 4mk: x = A₀e^{−bt/2m} cos(ωt + φ), ω = √(ω₀² − (b/2m)²)

nodes.label: Driven oscillator and resonance
nodes.symbol: mẍ + bẋ + kx = F₀ sin ωt
nodes.description: A damped oscillator pushed periodically settles into motion at the driving frequency; its amplitude peaks (resonance) when the driving frequency is near the natural one.
properties: steady state at the driving frequency

nodes.label: Wave
nodes.description: A disturbance that travels through a medium (mechanical wave) while each part of the medium only oscillates about its equilibrium; transverse or longitudinal.
nodes.math_structure: displacement field y(x, t) of the medium, ℝ × ℝ → ℝ (or a vector field in 3D)

nodes.label: Wavelength
nodes.description: Distance between adjacent identical points of a periodic wave.

nodes.label: Wave speed
nodes.description: Speed at which the disturbance propagates; set by the medium, not by the source.

nodes.label: Traveling wave function
nodes.description: A wave shape that moves without changing; a pulse is a single such disturbance and y = A sin(kx − ωt + φ) is the periodic case.
nodes.math_structure: function of the single variable x − vt (or x + vt); periodic case y = A sin(kx ∓ ωt + φ)

nodes.label: Wave number
nodes.description: Spatial angular frequency of a wave, in rad/m; v = ω/k.

nodes.label: Linear wave equation
nodes.description: The equation satisfied by every wave travelling at speed v in a linear medium.
properties: second order in x and t
general solution f(x − vt) + g(x + vt)

nodes.label: Wave power
nodes.description: Energy per unit time carried by a wave; proportional to the square of the amplitude and of the frequency.

nodes.label: Intensity
nodes.description: Power per unit area carried by a wave; for a spherical wave I = P/(4πr²).

nodes.label: Boundary conditions
nodes.description: At a fixed end the displacement is zero and a reflected pulse is inverted; at a free end the slope is zero and the pulse returns upright.
properties: partial reflection and transmission at a change of medium

nodes.label: Interference
nodes.description: Two overlapping waves add constructively (in phase, double amplitude) or destructively (half a cycle apart, cancel).
nodes.math_structure: superposed wave field; resultant amplitude 2A|cos(φ/2)| set by the phase difference φ

nodes.label: Superposition principle
nodes.description: When waves overlap, the displacements add; follows from the linearity of the wave equation.
properties: holds for small amplitudes in linear media
waves pass through each other unchanged

nodes.label: Standing wave
nodes.description: Two equal waves moving in opposite directions produce a pattern that does not travel: nodes stay at rest, antinodes oscillate most.
nodes.math_structure: product of a fixed spatial profile and a time oscillation; nodes at kx = nπ

nodes.label: Normal modes
nodes.description: A string fixed at both ends can only hold standing waves that fit its length: the fundamental and its overtones.
nodes.math_structure: discrete family n = 1, 2, 3, …; any motion is a superposition of modes

nodes.label: Sound wave
nodes.description: A longitudinal wave of compressions and rarefactions in a medium; the pressure wave is a quarter cycle out of phase with the displacement wave.
nodes.math_structure: pressure field Δp = Δp_max sin(kx ∓ ωt + φ) and displacement field s = s_max cos(kx ∓ ωt + φ)

nodes.label: Speed of sound
nodes.description: Set by an elastic property over an inertial property of the medium: √(B/ρ) in fluids, √(Y/ρ) in solids, √(γRT/M) in an ideal gas.

nodes.label: Sound intensity level
nodes.description: Logarithmic measure of intensity relative to the threshold I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m².

nodes.label: Air-column modes
nodes.description: Standing sound waves in a tube: open at both ends all harmonics f_n = nv/2L; closed at one end only odd ones, f_n = nv/4L.
nodes.math_structure: discrete modes; displacement antinode at an open end, node at a closed end

nodes.label: Beat frequency
nodes.description: Two sounds of slightly different frequency produce a loudness that rises and falls at the difference frequency.

nodes.label: Doppler-shifted frequency
nodes.description: The frequency heard changes when source or observer moves through the medium: higher when approaching, lower when receding.

nodes.label: Shock wave
nodes.description: A source faster than sound piles up its wavefronts on a cone; the pressure jump is heard as a sonic boom, and a boat's bow wake is the surface analogue.
nodes.math_structure: conical envelope of spherical wavefronts, half-angle θ with sin θ = v/v_s (Mach number M = v_s/v)

nodes.label: Temperature
nodes.description: How hot a body is, read from a thermometer; bodies in thermal equilibrium share one temperature. SI unit the kelvin.

nodes.label: Thermal equilibrium
nodes.description: The state reached by bodies in thermal contact when heat transfer between them has stopped.
nodes.math_structure: equivalence relation on equilibrium states of bodies in contact; its classes are labelled by temperature

nodes.label: Zeroth law
nodes.symbol: A ~ C, B ~ C ⇒ A ~ B
nodes.description: Two bodies each in thermal equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other.
properties: transitivity: thermal equilibrium is an equivalence relation

nodes.label: Temperature scales
nodes.description: Celsius and Fahrenheit are relative scales; the Kelvin scale is absolute, with zero at absolute zero and the triple point of water at 273.16 K.
properties: absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature
the kelvin and the degree Celsius have equal size

nodes.label: Thermal expansion
nodes.description: Most materials grow when heated: linearly in the temperature change for small changes; β ≈ 3α for isotropic solids. Water below 4 °C is an exception.

nodes.label: Thermal stress
nodes.description: Stress that appears when a body is prevented from expanding or contracting.

nodes.label: Heat
nodes.description: Energy transferred between bodies because of their temperature difference. 1 cal = 4.186 J (mechanical equivalent of heat).

nodes.label: Specific heat
nodes.description: Heat needed per unit mass to raise the temperature by one kelvin.

nodes.label: Calorimetry
nodes.description: Heat lost by the hot bodies in an insulated container equals heat gained by the cold ones.

nodes.label: Phase diagram
nodes.description: Which phase (solid, liquid, gas) is stable at each pressure and temperature; the coexistence lines meet at the triple point and the liquid–vapor line ends at the critical point.
nodes.math_structure: partition of the (p, T) plane by coexistence curves; triple point; critical point (T_c, p_c); vapor pressure curve

nodes.label: Latent heat
nodes.description: Heat absorbed or released at constant temperature during a phase change: heat of fusion, vaporization or sublimation.

nodes.label: Heat conduction
nodes.description: Heat flows through a material at a rate proportional to area and temperature difference and inversely to thickness.

nodes.label: Convection
nodes.description: Heat transported by bulk motion of a fluid, driven by buoyancy (natural) or by pumps and fans (forced).
properties: natural convection driven by density differences

nodes.label: Stefan–Boltzmann law
nodes.description: Every body radiates energy at a rate proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature; the net rate is σeA(T₂⁴ − T₁⁴).
book_terms: net rate of heat transfer by radiation

nodes.label: Ideal gas law
nodes.description: For a dilute gas, pressure times volume is proportional to the number of molecules and the absolute temperature (Boyle, Charles and Gay-Lussac combined).

nodes.label: Boltzmann constant
nodes.description: Converts temperature to energy per molecule: 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K.

nodes.label: Avogadro's number
nodes.description: Number of molecules in one mole, 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; the mole counts amount of substance.

nodes.label: Gas constant
nodes.description: Boltzmann's constant per mole: 8.31 J/(mol·K).

nodes.label: Van der Waals equation
nodes.description: Corrects the ideal gas law for attraction between molecules (a) and their own volume (b); predicts liquefaction below a critical temperature.
properties: reduces to the ideal gas law at low density
critical point where an isotherm has an inflection
book_terms: van der Waals equation of state

nodes.label: Equilibrium state of a gas
nodes.description: A gas in equilibrium is fixed by two of p, V, T; the third follows from the equation of state, so the state is a point on a pV diagram.
nodes.math_structure: point of the surface f(p, V, T) = 0; two coordinates suffice (a point of the pV plane)

nodes.label: Kinetic theory of gases
nodes.description: A gas is many point molecules in random motion; pressure is the momentum they transfer to the walls in collisions.

nodes.label: Internal energy
nodes.description: Total kinetic and potential energy of the molecules; for a monatomic ideal gas only kinetic, (3/2)Nk_BT.

nodes.label: rms speed
nodes.description: Square root of the mean square molecular speed.

nodes.label: Dalton's law
nodes.description: In a mixture each gas exerts its own partial pressure as if alone; the total pressure is their sum.
properties: molecules of ideal gases do not interact

nodes.label: Mean free path
nodes.description: Average distance a molecule travels between collisions; divided by the mean speed it gives the mean free time.

nodes.label: Molar heat capacity at constant volume
nodes.description: Heat per mole per kelvin at fixed volume.
book_terms: molar heat capacity at constant volume

nodes.label: Equipartition theorem
nodes.symbol: ½ k_B T per degree of freedom
nodes.description: In thermal equilibrium each quadratic term in a molecule's energy (degree of freedom) carries an average energy ½k_BT.
properties: fails at low temperature where quantum effects freeze degrees of freedom

nodes.label: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
nodes.description: The equilibrium distribution of molecular speeds in an ideal gas.
nodes.math_structure: probability density on speeds v ≥ 0: f(v) = (4/√π)(m/2k_BT)^{3/2} v² e^{−mv²/2k_BT}

nodes.label: Most probable speed
nodes.description: Speed at the peak of the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution; below the mean and rms speeds.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic system
nodes.description: A part of the world separated by a boundary from its surroundings (environment); closed if no matter crosses, open otherwise. In equilibrium a few variables describe it.
nodes.math_structure: macroscopic state given by intensive variables (p, T) and extensive variables (V, E_int, N); equilibrium = no change in time

nodes.label: Equation of state
nodes.description: A relation among the state variables of a system in equilibrium.
properties: one relation, so two variables fix the state
examples: ideal gas, van der Waals

nodes.label: Quasi-static process
nodes.description: A process slow enough that the system passes through a sequence of equilibrium states, so it is a curve on the pV diagram.
nodes.math_structure: continuous curve of equilibrium states in the state space

nodes.label: Work done by a gas
nodes.description: Work done by a system that changes volume; the area under the path on the pV diagram, so it depends on the path.

nodes.label: First law of thermodynamics
nodes.description: The change of internal energy equals the heat added to the system minus the work done by the system.
properties: E_int is a state function, Q and W are path-dependent

nodes.label: Thermodynamic processes
nodes.description: Paths with one quantity held fixed: T (isothermal), p (isobaric), V (isochoric), or no heat exchanged (adiabatic); a cyclic process returns to its start. A reversible process can be run backward through the same states.
nodes.math_structure: constrained curves in state space; cyclic = closed curve (ΔE_int = 0, W = enclosed area); reversible = quasi-static with no dissipation

nodes.label: Molar heat capacity at constant pressure
nodes.description: Heat per mole per kelvin at fixed pressure; larger than C_V because the gas also does work.
book_terms: molar heat capacity at constant pressure

nodes.label: Adiabatic process of an ideal gas
nodes.description: In a quasi-static adiabatic expansion the gas cools; pressure and volume follow pV^γ = constant with γ = C_p/C_V.
properties: steeper than the isotherm on a pV diagram

nodes.label: Irreversible process
nodes.description: A process that cannot be undone without leaving a change in the surroundings: friction, free expansion, heat flow across a finite temperature difference.
nodes.math_structure: path not made of equilibrium states, or with dissipation; its reverse is never observed spontaneously

nodes.label: Clausius statement
nodes.symbol: no spontaneous heat flow cold → hot
nodes.description: Heat never flows spontaneously from a colder to a hotter body; doing so requires work.
properties: one form of the second law
book_terms: Clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics

nodes.label: Heat engine
nodes.description: A device run in a cycle that takes heat Q_h from a hot reservoir, rejects Q_c to a cold reservoir and delivers the difference as work.
properties: first law fixes W = Q_h − Q_c

nodes.label: Efficiency
nodes.description: Fraction of the heat taken in that is turned into work.

nodes.label: Refrigerator and heat pump
nodes.description: An engine run backward: work moves heat from a cold reservoir to a hot one, to cool the cold side (refrigerator) or heat the hot side (heat pump).
properties: same energy balance as an engine

nodes.label: Coefficient of performance
nodes.description: Heat moved per work supplied; can exceed 1.

nodes.label: Kelvin statement
nodes.description: No cyclic process can convert heat from one reservoir entirely into work; equivalently there is no perfect engine (and, by the Clausius form, no perfect refrigerator).
book_terms: Kelvin statement of the second law of thermodynamics

nodes.label: Carnot cycle
nodes.description: A reversible cycle of two isothermal and two adiabatic steps between two reservoirs; an engine run on it is a Carnot engine.
nodes.math_structure: closed curve in the pV plane: isotherm at T_h, adiabat, isotherm at T_c, adiabat

nodes.label: Carnot principle
nodes.description: No engine between two reservoirs beats a reversible one, and all reversible engines between them have e = 1 − T_c/T_h.
properties: efficiency depends only on reservoir temperatures

nodes.label: Entropy
nodes.description: A state function whose change is the heat added reversibly divided by the absolute temperature.

nodes.label: Second law (entropy statement)
nodes.description: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; it stays constant only for reversible processes.
properties: equivalent to the Kelvin and Clausius statements
book_terms: entropy statement of the second law of thermodynamics

nodes.label: Third law
nodes.description: Entropy changes along an isotherm vanish as the temperature approaches absolute zero; absolute zero cannot be reached in a finite number of steps.

nodes.label: Electric charge
nodes.description: A property of matter that comes in two signs: like charges repel, unlike attract. Additive; SI unit the coulomb.

nodes.label: Conservation of charge
nodes.description: The total charge of an isolated system never changes; charging a body only moves charge from one body to another.
properties: local form is the continuity equation

nodes.label: Charge carriers
nodes.description: Ordinary charge is carried by electrons (−e) and protons (+e); neutrons are neutral. An ion has more or fewer electrons than protons.
nodes.math_structure: composition of matter: numbers of electrons, protons, neutrons; net charge (N_p − N_e)e, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C

nodes.label: Conductor
nodes.description: A material in which some electrons (conduction electrons) move freely; charge placed on it spreads out, and nearby charges can induce a separation (charging by induction).
nodes.math_structure: bulk with mobile charge density that rearranges in response to fields

nodes.label: Insulator
nodes.description: A material whose charges are bound to atoms; a field can only shift them slightly, polarizing the material into small dipoles.
nodes.math_structure: bulk with bound charges; response = polarization (displacement of bound charges)

nodes.label: Coulomb's law
nodes.description: Two point charges exert forces on each other along the line joining them, proportional to the product of the charges and inversely to the square of the distance.
properties: sign of q₁q₂ gives repulsion or attraction

nodes.label: Permittivity of vacuum
nodes.description: Constant in Coulomb's law, 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²); k = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².

nodes.label: Superposition of electric forces
nodes.description: The force from several charges is the vector sum of the forces each would exert alone.
properties: pairwise forces unaffected by other charges

nodes.label: Point-charge configuration
nodes.description: The simplest electrostatic state: which charges there are and where they sit.
nodes.math_structure: N points of ℝ³, each with a charge label q_i

nodes.label: Electric field
nodes.description: The field produced by source charges, defined at every point of space; a test charge there feels qE⃗.
nodes.math_structure: vector field on ℝ³ (away from point charges)

nodes.label: Field value
nodes.description: Force per unit test charge at a point; measured with a small test charge.

nodes.label: Continuous charge distribution
nodes.description: Charge spread along a line, over a surface or through a volume, described by a charge density; an infinite straight wire and an infinite plane are idealised cases.
nodes.math_structure: density function on a curve (λ), surface (σ) or region (ρ); dq = λ dl, σ dA, ρ dV

nodes.label: Field lines
nodes.description: Curves drawn tangent to the field, starting on positive and ending on negative charges, more crowded where the field is stronger.

nodes.label: Electric dipole moment
nodes.description: Charge times separation of a ± charge pair; molecules can have a permanent dipole or one induced by a field.

nodes.label: Electric flux
nodes.description: The amount of field passing through a surface: field component along the area vector (normal to the surface) times area, summed over the surface.

nodes.label: Gauss's law
nodes.description: The electric flux through any closed (Gaussian) surface equals the enclosed charge divided by ε₀.
properties: follows from Coulomb's law and superposition
charge outside contributes zero net flux

nodes.label: Symmetry method
nodes.description: With spherical, cylindrical or planar symmetry the field is constant on a well-chosen Gaussian surface, and Gauss's law gives it directly.

nodes.label: Conductor in electrostatic equilibrium
nodes.description: With charges at rest, the field inside a conductor is zero, excess charge sits on the surface, and just outside E = σ/ε₀ perpendicular to the surface.
nodes.math_structure: E⃗ = 0 in the bulk; surface charge σ; E⃗ ⟂ surface outside with magnitude σ/ε₀

nodes.label: Electric potential energy
nodes.description: Potential energy of a system of charges; the Coulomb force is conservative, so it exists.

nodes.label: Electric potential
nodes.description: Potential energy per unit charge at each point; a scalar field defined up to an additive constant.
nodes.math_structure: scalar field on ℝ³ modulo constants

nodes.label: Voltage
nodes.description: Potential difference between two points, measured with a voltmeter; SI unit the volt. qΔV is an energy (electron-volt for q = e).

nodes.label: Gradient
nodes.description: The vector of partial derivatives of a scalar field; points toward steepest increase.

nodes.label: Equipotential surfaces
nodes.description: Surfaces of constant potential; the field is perpendicular to them and no work is done moving a charge along one. A conductor's surface is one; grounding sets it to zero.

nodes.label: Capacitor
nodes.description: Two conductors carrying equal and opposite charges, often separated by a dielectric; the parallel-plate capacitor is the standard example.
nodes.math_structure: pair of conductors in electrostatic equilibrium with charges +Q, −Q; field confined mainly between them

nodes.label: Capacitance
nodes.description: Charge stored per volt of potential difference; depends only on geometry and the material between the conductors. SI unit the farad.

nodes.label: Capacitors in series and parallel
nodes.description: Capacitors in parallel share a voltage and their capacitances add; in series they share a charge and the inverses add.
properties: follows from charge conservation and additivity of potential differences

nodes.label: Energy stored in a capacitor
nodes.description: Work needed to charge a capacitor, stored in its electric field.

nodes.label: Electric energy density
nodes.description: Energy per unit volume stored in an electric field.

nodes.label: Dielectric constant
nodes.description: Factor by which an insulating material between the plates raises the capacitance and lowers the field.

nodes.label: Molecular model of a dielectric
nodes.description: The applied field induces or aligns molecular dipoles; the induced surface charges create an induced field that partly cancels the applied one.
properties: induced field opposite to the applied field

nodes.label: Dielectric strength
nodes.description: Largest field an insulator withstands before it breaks down and conducts.

nodes.label: Electric current
nodes.description: Rate at which charge passes a cross section; SI unit the ampere (1 A = 1 C/s). Conventional current points the way positive charge would move.

nodes.label: Electric circuit
nodes.description: A closed conducting path through sources and elements, drawn as a schematic; charge flows steadily only around closed paths.
nodes.math_structure: graph of elements joined at junctions; state = branch currents and capacitor charges

nodes.label: Drift velocity
nodes.description: Small average velocity of the charge carriers along a wire, superposed on their fast random motion.

nodes.label: Current density
nodes.description: Current per unit area at each point of a conductor; integrated over a cross section it gives the current.
nodes.math_structure: vector field on the conductor; I = ∫ J⃗·dA⃗

nodes.label: Resistivity
nodes.description: Material property: field needed per unit current density; its inverse is the electrical conductivity. It grows roughly linearly with temperature in metals.

nodes.label: Resistance
nodes.description: Voltage per current of a component; for a uniform wire R = ρL/A. SI unit the ohm.

nodes.label: Ohm's law
nodes.description: For many materials current is proportional to voltage with R independent of V (ohmic); devices such as diodes are nonohmic.

nodes.label: Electric power
nodes.description: Rate at which electrical energy is delivered to an element; in a resistor it becomes heat at I²R = V²/R.

nodes.label: Superconducting state
nodes.description: Below a critical temperature some materials lose all resistance and expel magnetic fields (Meissner effect); a quantum effect of electron pairs.
nodes.math_structure: macroscopic phase below T_c with ρ = 0 and B = 0 in the bulk

nodes.label: Electromotive force
nodes.description: Work per unit charge done by a source (battery, generator) in moving charge around a circuit; the voltage of the source with no current.

nodes.label: Terminal voltage
nodes.description: Voltage across a source's terminals; below its emf by the potential drop on its internal resistance.

nodes.label: Resistors in series and parallel
nodes.description: Resistors in series carry the same current and their resistances add; in parallel they share the voltage and the inverses add.

nodes.label: Kirchhoff's rules
nodes.description: Junction rule: current into a junction equals current out. Loop rule: the potential differences around any closed loop sum to zero.

nodes.label: Ammeter and voltmeter
nodes.symbol: series, small R / parallel, large R
nodes.description: An ammeter is placed in series and has very small resistance; a voltmeter is placed in parallel and has very large resistance, so neither disturbs the circuit much.

nodes.label: RC circuit
nodes.description: A capacitor charging or discharging through a resistor: charge and current change exponentially with time constant τ = RC.
properties: charging q → Cε, discharging q = Q e^{−t/RC}

nodes.label: Magnetic poles
nodes.description: Every magnet has a north and a south pole; like poles repel, unlike attract, and cutting a magnet never isolates a single pole.
nodes.math_structure: pair of poles of a magnetic dipole; no isolated monopoles observed

nodes.label: Magnetic force on a moving charge
nodes.description: A charge moving through a magnetic field feels a force perpendicular to both its velocity and the field (right-hand rule); the force does no work.
properties: does no work, changes only direction

nodes.label: Magnetic field
nodes.description: The field around magnets and currents, mapped by a compass; its field lines form closed loops. SI unit the tesla (1 G = 10⁻⁴ T).
nodes.math_structure: divergence-free vector field on ℝ³: field lines close on themselves

nodes.label: Magnetic field value
nodes.description: Field at one point, defined through the force on a moving test charge: B = F/(qv sin θ).

nodes.label: Circular and helical orbits
nodes.description: A charge in a uniform field moves on a circle of radius mv/(qB) with period 2πm/(qB); a velocity component along B⃗ turns the circle into a helix.
nodes.math_structure: helix around a field line: uniform circular motion in the plane ⟂ B⃗ plus uniform motion along B⃗

nodes.label: Magnetic dipole moment
nodes.description: Current times area of a loop (times the number of turns), along the loop's normal; a current loop is a magnetic dipole.

nodes.label: Hall voltage
nodes.description: Voltage across a current-carrying strip in a magnetic field, from carriers pushed to one side; its sign reveals the sign of the carriers.

nodes.label: Velocity selector
nodes.description: Crossed electric and magnetic fields pass undeflected only particles with speed E/B.

nodes.label: Biot–Savart law
nodes.description: Each element of a current contributes to the magnetic field in proportion to the current and inversely to the square of the distance, perpendicular to both element and line of sight.

nodes.label: Permeability of free space
nodes.description: Constant in the magnetic field laws, 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

nodes.label: Field of a long straight wire
nodes.description: Circles around the wire, falling inversely with distance (right-hand rule for its direction).

nodes.label: Force between parallel currents
nodes.description: Parallel currents attract and antiparallel currents repel; this force once defined the ampere.

nodes.label: Ampère's law
nodes.description: The line integral of the magnetic field around any closed loop equals μ₀ times the current through it.

nodes.label: Solenoid and toroid
nodes.description: A long coil has a nearly uniform field inside, B = μ₀nI, and almost none outside; a toroid confines its field, B = μ₀NI/(2πr).
nodes.math_structure: uniform axial field inside a long solenoid; azimuthal field inside a toroid, zero outside

nodes.label: Magnetism in matter
nodes.description: Atomic magnetic dipoles respond to a field: weakly along it (paramagnetic, χ > 0), weakly against it (diamagnetic, χ < 0), or strongly with domains and hysteresis (ferromagnetic).
properties: paramagnetic and diamagnetic linear with small χ

nodes.label: Magnetic flux
nodes.description: Amount of magnetic field through a surface; SI unit the weber.

nodes.label: Faraday's law
nodes.description: A changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an emf in it, whether the field, the area or the orientation changes.

nodes.label: Lenz's law
nodes.description: The induced emf drives a current whose magnetic field opposes the change of flux that produced it.

nodes.label: Motional emf
nodes.description: Emf in a conductor moving through a magnetic field.

nodes.label: Induced electric field
nodes.description: A changing magnetic field creates an electric field whose lines close on themselves; it is not conservative.
nodes.math_structure: nonconservative electric vector field with closed field lines

nodes.label: Eddy currents
nodes.description: Currents induced in a conductor moving in, or exposed to, a changing magnetic field; by Lenz's law they oppose the motion (magnetic damping).

nodes.label: Electric generator
nodes.description: A coil turning in a magnetic field produces a sinusoidal emf with peak NBAω; a motor's coil produces the same, called back emf.
properties: motors and generators are the same device run in reverse

nodes.label: Mutual inductance
nodes.description: Flux through one circuit per current in another; a changing current in one induces emf ε₂ = −M dI₁/dt in the other. SI unit the henry.

nodes.label: Self-inductance
nodes.description: A coil's own flux per unit of its current; a changing current induces ε = −L dI/dt that opposes the change. An inductor is a coil built for this.

nodes.label: Energy in an inductor
nodes.description: Work done against the back emf while the current builds up, stored in the magnetic field.

nodes.label: Magnetic energy density
nodes.description: Energy per unit volume stored in a magnetic field.

nodes.label: RL circuit
nodes.description: Current in a resistor–inductor circuit rises or decays exponentially with time constant τ_L = L/R.

nodes.label: LC circuit
nodes.description: Charge sloshes between a capacitor and an inductor; energy passes between electric and magnetic fields.

nodes.label: RLC circuit
nodes.description: Adding resistance damps the LC oscillation: underdamped, critically damped or overdamped as for a mechanical oscillator.

nodes.label: Alternating source
nodes.description: A source whose voltage (and current) reverses periodically; direct current (dc) flows one way only.
nodes.math_structure: sinusoidal function of time with amplitude V₀ and angular frequency ω

nodes.label: Phasors
nodes.description: Represents a sinusoid A sin(ωt + φ) as a vector of length A rotating at ω; sinusoids of one frequency add as vectors.

nodes.label: Capacitive reactance
nodes.description: Opposition of a capacitor to alternating current; current leads voltage by 90°.

nodes.label: rms current and voltage
nodes.description: Effective values of a sinusoid: the dc values that deliver the same average power.

nodes.label: Inductive reactance
nodes.description: Opposition of an inductor to alternating current; current lags voltage by 90°.

nodes.label: Impedance and phase angle
nodes.description: Total opposition of a series RLC circuit to ac, I₀ = V₀/Z; the phase angle φ = tan⁻¹((X_L − X_C)/R) is how far current lags voltage.

nodes.label: Average ac power
nodes.description: Power averaged over a cycle; only the resistor dissipates, and cos φ is the power factor.

nodes.label: AC resonance
nodes.description: Current in a series RLC circuit peaks when X_L = X_C; the quality factor measures how sharp the peak is (bandwidth Δω = ω₀/Q).

nodes.label: Transformer
nodes.description: Two coils on one iron core: the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, and the current ratio its inverse, so power is transmitted at high voltage and low current.

nodes.label: Maxwell's equations
nodes.description: Gauss's law for E⃗, Gauss's law for B⃗ (no monopoles), Faraday's law, and Ampère's law with Maxwell's displacement current; with the Lorentz force they complete classical electromagnetism.
properties: a changing E⃗ makes B⃗ as a changing B⃗ makes E⃗

nodes.label: Displacement current
nodes.description: Maxwell's term: a changing electric flux acts like a current in Ampère's law, needed where a capacitor interrupts the conduction current.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic field
nodes.description: The dynamical state of classical electromagnetism: electric and magnetic fields at every point and time, evolving by Maxwell's equations.
nodes.math_structure: pair of vector fields on space-time satisfying Maxwell's equations

nodes.label: Plane electromagnetic wave
nodes.description: A solution of Maxwell's equations in empty space: transverse electric and magnetic fields in phase, travelling at c = 1/√(ε₀μ₀).
nodes.math_structure: E_y = E₀ sin(kx − ωt), B_z = (E₀/c) sin(kx − ωt); transverse, in phase

nodes.label: Poynting vector
nodes.description: Energy flux of the electromagnetic field: energy per unit area per unit time, along the direction of propagation.

nodes.label: Radiation pressure
nodes.description: Pressure exerted by light because electromagnetic waves carry momentum U/c.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic spectrum
nodes.description: Electromagnetic waves of all wavelengths: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays, distinguished only by frequency.
nodes.math_structure: one-parameter family of plane waves labelled by frequency f (wavelength λ = c/f)

nodes.label: Index of refraction
nodes.description: Ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in a medium; at least 1.

nodes.label: Ray model of light
nodes.description: Geometric optics: light travels along straight rays in a uniform medium, bending only at boundaries. Valid when objects and apertures are much larger than the wavelength.
properties: rays straight in a uniform medium

nodes.label: Law of reflection
nodes.description: A ray reflects from a smooth surface at the same angle to the normal as it arrived, in the same plane.
properties: incident ray, normal and reflected ray coplanar

nodes.label: Law of refraction
nodes.symbol: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
nodes.description: A ray entering a medium of different index bends toward the normal if the new index is larger (Snell's law).
properties: bending set by the ratio of indices

nodes.label: Critical angle
nodes.description: Angle of incidence beyond which light going into a medium of lower index is totally reflected (total internal reflection).

nodes.label: Dispersion
nodes.description: The index of refraction depends on wavelength, so a prism spreads white light into colours.
properties: n decreases with λ in the visible for glass
different colours refract by different angles

nodes.label: Huygens's principle
nodes.description: Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; the new wavefront is their envelope. It explains reflection, refraction and diffraction (wave optics).
properties: wavelets travel at the local wave speed

nodes.label: Polarization
nodes.description: The direction of the electric field of light in the plane perpendicular to its travel: fixed for polarized light (vertically, horizontally…), random for unpolarized light.
nodes.math_structure: unit vector (direction of polarization) in the plane ⟂ k⃗; unpolarized = random mixture

nodes.label: Malus's law
nodes.description: A polarizing filter transmits the field component along its axis, so intensity falls as cos²θ.
properties: projection of E⃗ on the axis

nodes.label: Brewster's angle
nodes.description: Angle of incidence at which reflected light is completely polarized parallel to the surface.

nodes.label: Optical image
nodes.description: Where rays from a point of an object meet (real image, can be caught on a screen) or appear to come from (virtual image). A plane mirror forms a virtual image as far behind as the object is in front.
nodes.math_structure: point-to-point map from object positions (object distance d_o) to image positions (image distance d_i)

nodes.label: Mirror equation
nodes.description: For a curved (spherical) mirror and rays near the optical axis, object and image distances are related through the focal length f = R/2.
properties: focal point where parallel rays meet

nodes.label: Magnification
nodes.description: Image height over object height; negative for an inverted image.

nodes.label: Aberrations
nodes.description: Real mirrors and lenses do not bring all rays to one point: spherical aberration (rays far from the axis), coma (off-axis points), and others.
properties: appear where the small-angle approximation fails
reduced by aperture stops or aspheric shapes

nodes.label: Refraction at a curved surface
nodes.description: A single spherical boundary between media forms images; for a flat boundary it gives the apparent depth h_i = (n₂/n₁)h_o.
properties: object focus and image focus differ when n₁ ≠ n₂

nodes.label: Thin lens
nodes.description: Two refracting surfaces close together: converging lenses (f > 0) and diverging lenses (f < 0), with 1/f = (n₂/n₁ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) (lens maker's equation). Images are found by ray tracing.
properties: parallel rays meet in the focal plane
same form as the mirror equation

nodes.label: The eye as an optical system
nodes.description: The eye images onto the retina at fixed distance by changing its power (accommodation) between the near and far points; myopia and hyperopia are corrected with lenses.

nodes.label: Optical power
nodes.description: Inverse focal length in diopters (m⁻¹); powers of thin lenses in contact add.

nodes.label: Angular magnification
nodes.description: How much larger an object appears through an instrument than to the unaided eye at the near point; a simple magnifier gives at most 1 + 25 cm/f.

nodes.label: Microscope and telescope
nodes.description: Two-lens instruments: the objective forms a real image that the eyepiece magnifies; magnifications multiply.

nodes.label: Coherent light
nodes.description: Light waves whose phase difference stays constant (coherent), usually of one wavelength (monochromatic); incoherent light washes out interference.
nodes.math_structure: set of waves with time-independent relative phases; monochromatic = single frequency

nodes.label: Double-slit interference
nodes.description: Young's experiment: light from two slits forms bright fringes where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths (order m) and dark fringes halfway between.
nodes.math_structure: intensity pattern on a screen: bright at d sin θ = mλ, dark at d sin θ = (m + ½)λ; y_m = mλD/d

nodes.label: Multiple-slit interference
nodes.description: With N slits the principal maxima stay at d sin θ = mλ but become sharper, with N − 2 weak secondary maxima between them.
nodes.math_structure: intensity pattern with principal maxima at d sin θ = mλ and N − 2 secondary maxima in between

nodes.label: Thin-film interference
nodes.description: Light reflected from the top and bottom of a thin film interferes; a half-wavelength phase change on reflection from a higher-index medium decides which colours are reinforced (soap bubbles, Newton's rings).
nodes.math_structure: interference pattern set by thickness t, index n and reflection phase shifts

nodes.label: Michelson interferometer
nodes.description: Splits a beam, sends the halves along two arms and recombines them; moving one mirror by λ/2 shifts the pattern by one fringe.
properties: measures lengths in units of λ/2
sensitive to changes of optical path in either arm

nodes.label: Single-slit diffraction
nodes.description: Light spreads after passing a narrow slit; wavelets from different parts of the slit cancel at angles where a sin θ = mλ.
nodes.math_structure: intensity pattern with a broad central maximum and minima at a sin θ = mλ, m = ±1, ±2, …
book_terms: destructive interference for a single slit

nodes.label: Single-slit intensity
nodes.description: Intensity across the single-slit pattern, β = πa sin θ/λ; the central peak's width is set by λ/a.

nodes.label: Two-slit diffraction pattern
nodes.description: With slits of finite width, the double-slit fringes are modulated by the single-slit envelope; fringes falling on envelope minima are missing orders.
nodes.math_structure: product of the double-slit interference intensity and the single-slit diffraction envelope

nodes.label: Diffraction grating
nodes.description: Thousands of equally spaced slits give very sharp principal maxima, so a grating separates wavelengths precisely.
properties: sharpness grows with the number of lines

nodes.label: Rayleigh criterion
nodes.description: Two point sources are just resolved when the central maximum of one falls on the first minimum of the other; diffraction limits every optical instrument's resolution.

nodes.label: Bragg's law
nodes.description: X-rays reflected from successive planes of atoms in a crystal (Bragg planes) interfere constructively when the extra path 2d sin θ is a whole number of wavelengths.
properties: measures atomic spacings d ~ λ of X-rays

nodes.label: Holography
nodes.description: A hologram records the interference of object light with a reference beam, storing amplitude and phase; illuminated again, it reconstructs a three-dimensional image.
properties: records phase as well as intensity

nodes.label: Special relativity
nodes.description: Einstein's theory of space and time for inertial frames, built on two postulates; it reconciles mechanics with electromagnetism.
properties: reduces to Newtonian mechanics for v ≪ c

nodes.label: First postulate
nodes.symbol: same laws in all inertial frames
nodes.description: The laws of physics, including electromagnetism, have the same form in every inertial frame.
properties: extends Galilean relativity from mechanics to all physics

nodes.label: Michelson–Morley result
nodes.description: An interferometer turned relative to Earth's motion showed no change in the speed of light: there is no detectable motion through an ether.

nodes.label: Second postulate
nodes.symbol: c the same in all inertial frames
nodes.description: Light in vacuum travels at c in every inertial frame, whatever the motion of source or observer.

nodes.label: Relativity of simultaneity
nodes.symbol: t_A = t_B in S ⇏ in S′
nodes.description: Two events simultaneous in one inertial frame are generally not simultaneous in another moving relative to it.
properties: consequence of the invariance of c

nodes.label: Time dilation
nodes.description: A clock moving relative to an observer runs slow: the time between two events at one place in the clock's frame (proper time Δτ) is the shortest.

nodes.label: Lorentz factor
nodes.description: Factor that measures how far relativistic effects depart from Newtonian ones; 1 at rest, infinite at c.

nodes.label: Length contraction
nodes.description: A body is shortest in its own rest frame (proper length L₀); moving, it is shorter along the motion.

nodes.label: Lorentz transformation
nodes.symbol: x′ = γ(x − vt),  t′ = γ(t − vx/c²)
nodes.description: Converts the coordinates of an event between two inertial frames so that the speed of light is the same in both.
properties: preserves the interval (Δs)² = Δx² + Δy² + Δz² − c²Δt²
reduces to the Galilean transformation for v ≪ c

nodes.label: Space-time
nodes.description: The four-dimensional arena of special relativity; a particle's history is a world line, and the interval between events is the same in all frames.
nodes.math_structure: Minkowski space ℝ⁴ with interval (Δs)² = Δx² + Δy² + Δz² − c²Δt²; world lines are curves in it

nodes.label: Relativistic velocity addition
nodes.description: Velocities combine so that no sum of speeds below c ever exceeds c; for slow speeds this reduces to classical (Galilean) velocity addition.
properties: reduces to u = u′ + v for v, u′ ≪ c
c combined with any v gives c

nodes.label: Relativistic Doppler effect
nodes.description: The frequency of light from a receding source is lower (red shift), from an approaching one higher; it depends only on the relative velocity.

nodes.label: Relativistic momentum
nodes.description: The momentum conserved in all inertial frames; m is the rest mass, the same in every frame.

nodes.label: Relativistic kinetic energy
nodes.description: Work needed to bring a body from rest to speed u; it grows without bound as u → c, so no massive body reaches c.

nodes.label: Total energy and rest energy
nodes.description: Total energy of a body: kinetic energy plus its rest energy mc²; mass is a form of energy. E² = (pc)² + (mc²)².

nodes.label: Blackbody radiation
nodes.description: Radiation in equilibrium with a perfect absorber and emitter at temperature T; its spectrum depends only on T, peaking at λ_max with λ_max T = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K (Wien).
nodes.math_structure: spectral power intensity I(λ, T) on λ > 0, one curve per temperature

nodes.label: Planck's constant
nodes.description: The quantum of action, 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s; it sets the scale at which energy comes in discrete amounts.

nodes.label: Planck's hypothesis
nodes.description: The oscillators exchanging energy with cavity radiation can only have energies that are whole multiples of hf.
properties: reduces to equipartition when hf ≪ k_BT
book_terms: quantum state of a Planck’s oscillator

nodes.label: Photoelectron energy
nodes.description: Light on a metal ejects photoelectrons (photocurrent from the photoelectrode); their maximum kinetic energy is measured by the stopping potential.

nodes.label: Cut-off frequency
nodes.description: Below a cut-off frequency (above a cut-off wavelength) no electrons are emitted, however intense the light.

nodes.label: Photon
nodes.description: A quantum of the electromagnetic field: energy hf, momentum h/λ along the propagation vector, zero rest mass. The photoelectric effect is a quantum phenomenon.
nodes.math_structure: particle of electromagnetic radiation: energy hf, momentum ħk⃗, E = pc

nodes.label: Work function
nodes.description: Minimum energy needed to free an electron from a metal's surface.

nodes.label: Compton shift
nodes.description: X-rays scattered by electrons come out with longer wavelength, by an amount fixed by the scattering angle; λ_c = h/(m₀c) = 0.00243 nm is the Compton wavelength.

nodes.label: Hydrogen line spectrum
nodes.description: Hydrogen emits and absorbs only at discrete wavelengths (Fraunhofer lines in sunlight), in series named Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund and Humphreys.

nodes.label: Nuclear model of the atom
nodes.description: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment showed that nearly all of an atom's mass and its positive charge sit in a tiny nucleus, with electrons far outside.
nodes.math_structure: point-like positive nucleus (radius ~10⁻¹⁵ m) with electrons at ~10⁻¹⁰ m

nodes.label: Bohr's model
nodes.description: Postulates for hydrogen: the electron moves only on orbits with angular momentum nħ, does not radiate on them, and emits or absorbs a photon when it jumps between them.
properties: quantization of angular momentum (quantum number n)
book_terms: Bohr’s model of the hydrogen atom

nodes.label: Hydrogen energy levels
nodes.description: The allowed states of Bohr's atom: radii r_n = a₀n² (Bohr radius a₀ = 0.529 Å) and energies −E₀/n²; ground state −13.6 eV, ionization energy 13.6 eV. Hydrogen-like ions scale with Z.
nodes.math_structure: discrete levels n = 1, 2, …; E_n = −Z²E₀/n², r_n = a₀n²/Z
book_terms: ground state energy of the hydrogen atom
excited energy states of the H atom
ionization limit of the hydrogen atom

nodes.label: de Broglie's hypothesis
nodes.description: Every particle has an associated matter wave (de Broglie wave) with wavelength h/p; the wave packet moves at the group velocity, which equals the particle's velocity.
properties: wavelength significant only at atomic scales
book_terms: de Broglie’s hypothesis of matter waves

nodes.label: Electron diffraction
nodes.description: Davisson and Germer saw electrons diffracted by a nickel crystal with the angles of Bragg's law, confirming λ = h/p.

nodes.label: Wave–particle duality
nodes.description: Light and matter both show wave behaviour (interference in the double-slit interference experiment) and particle behaviour (single detections); neither picture alone suffices.
properties: single quanta build up an interference pattern

nodes.label: Uncertainty principle
nodes.description: Position and momentum cannot both be sharp: the product of their uncertainties is at least ħ/2.
properties: a property of waves (Fourier pairs), not of measuring apparatus

nodes.label: Wave function
nodes.description: The quantum state of a particle: a complex function of position and time; its symmetry under x → −x may be even or odd.
nodes.math_structure: complex square-integrable function on configuration space (element of L²), defined up to a global phase

nodes.label: Born rule
nodes.description: |Ψ(x, t)|² is the probability density for finding the particle at x; the total probability is one (normalization condition).

nodes.label: Measurement and state reduction
nodes.description: A measurement gives one definite outcome, and the wave function is then replaced by one consistent with it (wave function collapse, Copenhagen interpretation).
properties: discontinuous change of state on measurement

nodes.label: Expectation value
nodes.description: Average of many measurements on identically prepared systems; position and momentum act as operators x and −iħ ∂/∂x.

nodes.label: Correspondence principle
nodes.description: In the limit of large energies (large quantum numbers) quantum predictions agree with classical mechanics.

nodes.label: Wave packet
nodes.description: A localised wave made by superposing plane waves of nearby wave numbers; the narrower it is in x, the broader in k.
nodes.math_structure: superposition of plane waves with amplitude A(k); Δx Δk ≥ ½

nodes.label: Energy–time uncertainty
nodes.description: A state that lasts only Δt has an energy spread at least ħ/(2Δt); short-lived states have broad lines.
properties: E = ħω and Δω Δt ≥ ½

nodes.label: Schrödinger equation
nodes.description: The equation of motion of the wave function: given Ψ at one time and the potential energy U, it fixes Ψ at all times.

nodes.label: Time-independent Schrödinger equation
nodes.description: For a potential that does not change in time, Ψ = ψ(x)e^{−iωt}; ψ satisfies an eigenvalue equation for the energy, and e^{−iωt} is the time-modulation factor.

nodes.label: Particle in a box
nodes.description: A particle confined to an infinite square well: ψ_n = √(2/L) sin(nπx/L), standing matter waves; only discrete energy levels with quantum number n ≥ 1 are allowed, so even the ground state energy is nonzero.
nodes.math_structure: discrete set of states ψ_n, n = 1, 2, 3, …; energies ∝ n²
