nodes.label: Stationary state
nodes.description: A solution with one definite energy; its probability density does not change, so it is a standing wave state.
nodes.math_structure: Ψ_n = ψ_n(x) e^{−iE_nt/ħ}

nodes.label: Quantum harmonic oscillator
nodes.description: The Schrödinger equation with U = ½mω²x²: equally spaced levels, a zero-point energy ħω/2, and wave functions built from Hermite polynomials.
nodes.math_structure: states ψ_n = N_n e^{−β²x²/2} H_n(βx), n = 0, 1, 2, …

nodes.label: Tunneling probability
nodes.description: A particle can cross a potential barrier higher than its energy; the transmission probability falls exponentially with barrier width and with √(U₀ − E).

nodes.label: Hydrogen atom
nodes.description: Solutions of the Schrödinger equation for the Coulomb potential: atomic orbitals labelled by n, l (0 … n − 1) and m (−l … l). Energies depend only on n and agree with Bohr's; electrons have no definite orbits.
nodes.math_structure: eigenfunctions ψ_nlm(r, θ, φ); n ≥ 1, 0 ≤ l < n, |m| ≤ l; radial probability density P(r) = 4πr²|ψ|²

nodes.label: Quantized angular momentum
nodes.description: Magnitude and one component of orbital angular momentum take only discrete values.

nodes.label: Orbital magnetic moment
nodes.description: The orbiting electron is a current loop; its moment comes in units of the Bohr magneton μ_B = eħ/2m_e.

nodes.label: Zeeman effect
nodes.description: In a magnetic field, levels with different m split, and spectral lines split into several components.

nodes.label: Electron spin
nodes.description: Intrinsic angular momentum of the electron, s = ½ with m_s = ±½, shown by the two beams of the Stern–Gerlach experiment; it carries a magnetic moment (e/m_e)S⃗.

nodes.label: Spin–orbit and hyperfine coupling
nodes.description: The electron's spin moment interacts with the field of its orbital motion (fine structure) and with the nuclear spin (hyperfine structure, spin-flip transitions such as hydrogen's 21-cm line).
properties: splits levels of equal n and l
small compared with the Coulomb energy

nodes.label: Pauli exclusion principle
nodes.description: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of quantum numbers (n, l, m, m_s).

nodes.label: Electron configuration
nodes.description: Electrons fill subshells in order of energy, each with at most 4l + 2; the outermost (valence) electrons fix chemical groups and the transition metals.
nodes.math_structure: occupation numbers of subshells (n, l) consistent with the exclusion principle

nodes.label: Selection rules
nodes.description: Atomic transitions that emit or absorb a photon change l by one, because the photon carries one unit of angular momentum.

nodes.label: Atomic X-rays
nodes.description: Heavy atoms emit characteristic X-ray lines when an inner vacancy is filled, with frequencies following Moseley's law; a continuous braking-radiation spectrum accompanies them.

nodes.label: Laser
nodes.description: An incoming photon stimulates an excited atom to emit an identical photon; with more atoms in an excited metastable state than below it (population inversion) the light is amplified into coherent, monochromatic light.
properties: stimulated photon has same frequency, phase, direction

nodes.label: Molecular bonds
nodes.description: Atoms bind by transferring an electron (ionic bond, energy set by ionization energy, electron affinity and Coulomb attraction), by sharing a pair of electrons in an antisymmetric spin state (covalent bond, exchange symmetry, hybridization), or by induced dipoles (van der Waals bond).
properties: equilibrium separation where U(r) is minimum
dissociation energy = depth of the minimum
covalent bonding needs the exclusion principle

nodes.label: Molecular energy levels
nodes.description: A diatomic molecule rotates and vibrates with quantized energies; electric dipole transitions obey Δl = ±1 and Δn = ±1, giving band spectra.
nodes.math_structure: rotational levels E_r = l(l+1)ħ²/(2I), I = μr₀²; vibrational levels (n + ½)ħω

nodes.label: Crystal lattice
nodes.description: Atoms or ions in a solid arranged in a repeating lattice (simple cubic, body-centered cubic, face-centered cubic); the Madelung constant sums the Coulomb energy of an ionic crystal, and a repulsion constant sets the short-range repulsion.
nodes.math_structure: periodic arrangement (Bravais lattice with a basis) with translational symmetry

nodes.label: Free electron gas
nodes.description: Conduction electrons as particles in a three-dimensional box, filling the lowest states two per level (exclusion principle) up to the Fermi energy; occupation at temperature T follows the Fermi factor.
nodes.math_structure: filled set of box states up to E_F; density of states g(E) ∝ E^{1/2}; Fermi temperature T_F = E_F/k_B

nodes.label: Energy bands
nodes.description: In a crystal the atomic levels broaden into energy bands separated by energy gaps; a filled valence band with a large gap gives an insulator, a small gap a semiconductor, a partly filled band a conductor.
nodes.math_structure: allowed energy intervals (valence band, conduction band) separated by forbidden gaps

nodes.label: Doped semiconductor
nodes.description: Impurity atoms add donor levels (n-type, extra electrons) or acceptor levels (p-type, holes) in the gap; the majority carrier sets the type, and the Hall effect shows its sign.
nodes.math_structure: band structure with impurity bands near the conduction band (donors) or the valence band (acceptors); carrier densities of electrons and holes

nodes.label: p–n junction
nodes.description: Joining p- and n-type material creates a depletion layer with a built-in field; current flows easily in forward bias and hardly at all in reverse bias, until breakdown.
nodes.math_structure: depletion layer with built-in potential; current–voltage relation I = I₀(e^{eV_b/k_BT} − 1)

nodes.label: Junction transistor
nodes.description: Two junctions back to back: a small base current controls a large collector current, so the device amplifies.

nodes.label: Critical magnetic field
nodes.description: Field above which superconductivity is destroyed; type I superconductors switch abruptly, type II pass through a mixed state.

nodes.label: BCS theory
nodes.description: Lattice vibrations bind electrons into Cooper pairs, which condense into one quantum state that carries current without resistance.

nodes.label: Nuclide
nodes.description: A nucleus specified by its atomic number Z (protons) and neutron number N; mass number A = Z + N counts nucleons. Isotopes share Z. Radius r = r₀A^{1/3}; masses in atomic mass units.
nodes.math_structure: pair (Z, N) of nucleon numbers; chart of the nuclides plots N against Z

nodes.label: Strong nuclear force
nodes.description: Attraction between nucleons, much stronger than the Coulomb repulsion at about 1 fm but negligible beyond a few fm.

nodes.label: Binding energy
nodes.description: Energy needed to separate a nucleus into its nucleons, equal to the mass defect times c²; binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron.

nodes.label: Radioactive decay law
nodes.description: Unstable nuclei decay at random with a constant probability λ per unit time, so their number and activity fall exponentially: half-life T½ = 0.693/λ, mean lifetime 1/λ.
properties: activity A = λN in becquerel (1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq)

nodes.label: Radioactive dating
nodes.description: Ages from the fraction of a radioactive isotope left, as in carbon-14 dating of once-living material.
properties: range limited to a few half-lives

nodes.label: Nuclear decays
nodes.description: A parent nucleus becomes a daughter: α decay emits a helium nucleus, β⁻ decay an electron and an antineutrino, β⁺ decay a positron (antielectron) and a neutrino, γ decay a photon from an excited nucleus. Heavy nuclei decay in series; transuranic elements are made artificially.
nodes.math_structure: transitions (Z, N) → (Z − 2, N − 2) + α; (Z + 1, N − 1) + e⁻ + ν̄; (Z − 1, N + 1) + e⁺ + ν; excited → ground + γ

nodes.label: Fission
nodes.description: A heavy nucleus such as ²³⁵U splits after absorbing a neutron, releasing about 200 MeV and further neutrons; a chain reaction is critical when each fission causes one more on average (critical mass).
nodes.math_structure: reaction n + ²³⁵U → fragments + 2–3 n + energy; chain reaction with multiplication factor k (k = 1 critical)

nodes.label: Liquid drop model
nodes.description: Treats the nucleus as a drop of incompressible nuclear fluid held by surface tension (strong force) and pushed apart by Coulomb repulsion; deformation splits a heavy drop.
properties: binding from volume, surface and Coulomb terms

nodes.label: Fusion
nodes.description: Light nuclei combine and release energy; in the Sun four protons become helium by the proton–proton chain. Stars build heavier elements (nucleosynthesis).
nodes.math_structure: reactions such as ¹H + ¹H → ²H + e⁺ + ν; proton–proton chain 4¹H → ⁴He + 2e⁺ + 2ν + energy

nodes.label: Radiation dose
nodes.description: Energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue (rad), weighted by the relative biological effectiveness of the radiation to give the equivalent dose (rem, sievert).

nodes.label: Fundamental forces
nodes.description: Four fundamental forces, each carried by bosons: gluons (strong), photons (electromagnetic), W and Z bosons (weak), gravitons (gravity, unobserved). The electromagnetic and weak forces unify into the electroweak force; grand unified theories and a theory of everything are sought.

nodes.label: Elementary particles
nodes.description: Matter is made of fermions (half-integer spin): leptons such as the electron and neutrino, and quarks, which form hadrons (baryons from three quarks, mesons from a quark and an antiquark). Every particle has an antiparticle, such as the positron. Bosons carry the forces.
nodes.math_structure: classification by spin (fermion/boson), charges and quantum numbers; antiparticles with opposite charges; exchange symmetry antisymmetric for fermions

nodes.label: Particle conservation laws
nodes.description: Reactions conserve charge, baryon number and lepton number; strangeness is conserved by the strong and electromagnetic forces but not the weak force.
properties: forbid reactions such as p → e⁺ + γ

nodes.label: Quark model
nodes.description: Hadrons are built from quarks with fractional charges; a new quantum number, color, lets three identical quarks share a state, and only colourless combinations exist.

nodes.label: Standard Model
nodes.description: The theory of the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces: forces arise from the exchange of virtual particles, pictured in Feynman diagrams; quantum electrodynamics (QED) and quantum chromodynamics (QCD) are its parts.
properties: virtual bosons exchanged within ΔE Δt ≥ ħ/2
range ~ ħ/(mc) for a carrier of mass m

nodes.label: Hubble's law
nodes.description: Distant galaxies recede with speeds proportional to their distance, measured from the redshift of their light; H₀ is Hubble's constant.

nodes.label: Big Bang model
nodes.description: The universe expanded from an extremely hot, dense early state; cosmology studies this history.
properties: expansion of space, not motion through it
hot early universe cooled as it expanded

nodes.label: Cosmic microwave background
nodes.description: Radiation left from the hot early universe, now a nearly uniform blackbody spectrum at 2.7 K in the microwave range.

nodes.label: Dark matter and dark energy
nodes.description: Galaxies rotate too fast for their visible mass (dark matter), and the expansion is accelerating (dark energy); together they make up most of the universe's energy.

routes.formula: base units s, m, kg (with A, K, mol, cd)
routes.title: Base quantities
routes.description: The unit system is built on base quantities; time, length and mass are the three used throughout mechanics.

routes.title: From the unit definitions
routes.description: Equalities between units in the SI give ratios equal to one.

routes.title: Dimension of a quantity
routes.description: Each quantity is assigned the exponents of the base quantities in its unit.

routes.formula: Q ≈ Π (rough inputs)^(powers fixed by dimension)
routes.title: Fermi estimate
routes.description: Rough inputs combined so the dimensions match, rounded to a power of ten.

routes.formula: A_measured − A_accepted, in the units of A
routes.title: Compare with the accepted value
routes.description: Measures accuracy, i.e. closeness to the accepted value.

routes.title: Stated with the value
routes.description: A measured quantity is reported as a value with its uncertainty, in the units of the quantity.

routes.title: First-order expansion
routes.description: Neglecting the product of two small uncertainties leaves the sum of percent uncertainties.

routes.formula: result digits limited by the least precise input
routes.title: Rounding rule
routes.description: A coarse version of propagation that is applied digit by digit.

routes.title: Geometric sum
routes.description: Defined by placing vectors tail to head; the order and grouping do not change the resultant.

routes.title: Scaling
routes.description: A scalar changes the length (and possibly the sense) of a vector but not its line.

routes.formula: A⃗ = A_x î + A_y ĵ + A_z k̂
routes.title: Decomposition along axes
routes.description: Every vector is a sum of scaled unit vectors of the axes; the scale factors are the scalar components.

routes.formula: x = r cos φ, y = r sin φ
routes.title: From Cartesian components
routes.description: The magnitude and direction angle of the position vector in the plane.

routes.formula: A⃗·B⃗ = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z = AB cos φ
routes.title: Component formula
routes.description: The geometric definition evaluated with orthonormal unit vectors.

routes.formula: A⃗×B⃗ = (A_yB_z − A_zB_y) î + (A_zB_x − A_xB_z) ĵ + (A_xB_y − A_yB_x) k̂
routes.title: Component formula
routes.description: Follows from the products of the unit vectors and distributivity.

routes.title: Coordinates and clock
routes.description: Positions are components along the frame's axes; instants are read from its clock.

routes.formula: x = signed distance from the origin
routes.title: Read on the axis
routes.description: A length measured along the axis from the origin, with a sign for the side.

routes.title: Position as a function of time
routes.description: Recording the position at each instant gives the motion.

routes.formula: Δx = x_f − x_i;  Δx_total = Σ Δx_i
routes.title: Difference of positions
routes.description: Taken from the motion at the end and start of the interval.

routes.title: Sum of magnitudes
routes.description: Adds the magnitudes of the displacements of each leg.

routes.title: Difference of clock readings
